data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's 'Economic Convergence' attack is a misuse of the word 'strictly': it only argues that small operators tend toward market-driven homogeneity. The problem asks whether a large service with STRICTLY MORE total internal redundancy is more resilient than the decentralized network. A large service is subject to identical economic-convergence incentives — it likewise uses AWS/Kubernetes/industry-standard libraries. SRC_002's 'global kill-switch' vulnerability applies equally, without differential force, to the large monolith. Since the large service has strictly more total internal redundancy on the same common substrate, the mere existence of shared standard tooling does not make the small operators MORE prone; it neutralizes the scale difference and leaves the large service with an edge. SRC_002 never identifies a reason economic convergence bites small operators harder (e.g., their inability to afford independent verification stacks), so its evidence only distinguishes correlated-from-independent failures in general, not the targeted comparison.
